_about: Held back from the published site until Finance and Compliance review them (HANDOFF decisions 20 and 21; the organization's rule: federal grant work needs that review before external communication). Nothing here is deleted. What is held: the Spanish text of the WCRP layer (CDBG-funded program: its popup, its legend line, its subtitle and the title of its file in the dictionary) and of Table 10 of the housing page (LIHTC projects funded with CDBG-DR: its cost and beneficiary columns and the groups of beneficiaries; the generic labels Project, Location, Type, Units, its note and its tag stay in Spanish), the headline figure of the Public money card, and the Spanish summaries (dictionary_plain, by entry id) of the dictionary entries of the WCRP layer and of Table 10. 'spanish' is the translation of each string, which the Spanish pages do not show: the line in i18n_src/es/<scope>.json repeats the English text instead. 'titles' is the Spanish title that a record of dictionary_src/datasets.json had; its 'es' now repeats the English title. 'headlines' is the headline figure that dictionary_src/domains.json had for a domain before it was set to null. To release a string: put its Spanish back in i18n_src/es/<scope>.json, delete it here and from i18n_src/keep.json, run python i18n.py, and raise the ?v= of js/i18n.js on the pages that use the scope. To release a title: put the Spanish back in datasets.json, delete it here, run python dictionary.py, python catalog.py and python registry.py. To release a headline: put the object back in domains.json, delete it here, run the same three commands, and python dictionary.py --domains. To release a dictionary summary: move it back to i18n_src/dictionary_plain.json, delete it here and run python dictionary.py. 'released' lists what was released on purpose after the hold, with who, when and why; the safety-net tests accept those strings.

public_spending_after.Each CDBG-DR and CDBG-MIT grant to the D: Cada subvención CDBG-DR y CDBG-MIT al Departamento de la Vivienda: lo que HUD obligó durante la vida de la subvención y lo que el Tesoro ha desembolsado al Departamento hasta ahora (sus giros), según USAspending. Los informes mensuales de HUD al 1 de septiembre de 2026 dan giros con una diferencia de 2 % o menos para cuatro de las seis subvenciones de más de $100 millones, y menores para la subvención de mitigación (4 %) y la de los terremotos de 2020 (19 %); USAspending se leyó después, en noviembre de 2026. Un giro le paga al Departamento, todavía no a la obra; una subvención firmada más tarde ha tenido menos tiempo para girar.
public_spending_after.The Department of Housing manages the fe: El Departamento de la Vivienda administra las subvenciones federales de recuperación y mitigación por desastres del programa Community Development Block Grant (CDBG-DR y CDBG-MIT). USAspending ubica esas subvenciones donde está el Departamento, en San Juan. La parte que el Departamento entrega como subadjudicaciones, a municipios, contratistas y organizaciones sin fines de lucro, se informa donde se hace el trabajo. Este mapa muestra esas subadjudicaciones.

public_spending.<b>Read with care.</b> A large project,: Lea con cuidado. Un proyecto grande, como una planta de tratamiento de agua que sirve a una región, cae en el único municipio donde se construye, por lo que algunos municipios sobresalen por residente. El mapa muestra dónde se construye un proyecto, no quién administra el dinero (a menudo una agencia central) ni quién se beneficia. Parte del programa es dinero federal (FEMA, HUD, fondos rotatorios de la EPA) que otras fuentes también informan: nunca lo sume a ellas.

public_money.HUD's Community Development Block Grants: Las Subvenciones en Bloque para el Desarrollo Comunitario de HUD llegan a Puerto Rico de tres formas. Las de recuperación y mitigación por desastres (CDBG-DR y CDBG-MIT) van al Departamento de la Vivienda de Puerto Rico: HUD obligó 19.10 mil millones de dólares en los años fiscales federales 2019 a 2025, y el Departamento informó 4.90 mil millones en subadjudicaciones a municipios, contratistas y organizaciones sin fines de lucro, 4.33 mil millones con un municipio. Las anuales van directo de HUD a 27 municipios más grandes (subvenciones de derecho o entitlement, 222 millones) y, para los demás municipios, al Departamento de la Vivienda como programa estatal CDBG (160 millones), que las transfiere como subadjudicaciones. Las subadjudicaciones suelen llegar un año o más después de la subvención, así que el último año puede mostrar poco. Obligado no es gastado. Seleccione el título de una columna para ordenar.
public_money.HUD's grants are placed through the suba: Las subvenciones de HUD se ubican por las subadjudicaciones que informa el Departamento de la Vivienda de Puerto Rico, y las subvenciones anuales de derecho (entitlement) por el municipio que las recibe. El dinero que el Departamento conserva para sus propios programas, aún no ha transferido o informa sin municipio no está ubicado.
public_money.The page also shows HUD's Community Deve: La página también muestra las Subvenciones en Bloque para el Desarrollo Comunitario (CDBG) de HUD: las de recuperación y mitigación por desastres (CDBG-DR y CDBG-MIT) y las anuales, según se obligaron en los años fiscales federales 2019 a 2025. El dinero de HUD nunca se suma al de FEMA: los años se cuentan de otra forma. Selecciónelo en Dinero o vea la sección 4.

study.table_10.en: Table 10 lists six housing projects named in the 2023 study. Each uses the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) and also gets money from the Community Development Block Grant for Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR), a program of the US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). The projects have 851 units in four municipalities. The study estimates their cost at $242,090,072 and their CDBG-DR grants at $90,532,871.
study.table_10.es: La Tabla 10 presenta seis proyectos de vivienda mencionados en el estudio de 2023. Cada uno usa el LIHTC (Crédito Contributivo por Vivienda de Bajos Ingresos) y además recibe dinero del CDBG-DR (Subvención en Bloque para el Desarrollo Comunitario, Recuperación ante Desastres), un programa de HUD (Departamento de Vivienda y Desarrollo Urbano federal). Los proyectos tienen 851 unidades en cuatro municipios. El estudio estima su costo en $242,090,072 y sus subvenciones de CDBG-DR en $90,532,871.

economy.fed_awards_total.en: Federal money promised for work or benefits in a municipality in one fiscal year (October to September). It adds contracts, grants, direct payments, loans (at their estimated cost) and other aid. It is not money spent and does not measure need. San Juan's figure can include money meant for the whole island. The Puerto Rico figure also counts awards that name no municipality.
economy.fed_awards_total.es: Fondos federales prometidos para trabajos o beneficios en un municipio en un año fiscal (de octubre a septiembre). Suma contratos, subvenciones, pagos directos, préstamos (según su costo estimado) y otras ayudas. No es dinero gastado y no mide la necesidad. La cifra de San Juan puede incluir dinero destinado a toda la isla. La cifra de Puerto Rico también cuenta las adjudicaciones que no nombran un municipio.

economy.fed_contracts.en: A federal contract is an agreement to pay a company or agency for goods or services. This is the money the government promised for contract work in the municipality in one fiscal year (October to September). It is money promised, not money spent. It can be negative when an earlier contract amount is cut.
economy.fed_contracts.es: Un contrato federal es un acuerdo para pagarle a una empresa o agencia por bienes o servicios. Esta cifra es el dinero que el gobierno prometió para trabajo por contrato en el municipio en un año fiscal (de octubre a septiembre). Es dinero prometido, no gastado. Puede ser negativa cuando se reduce el monto de un contrato anterior.

economy.fed_grants.en: Federal grants, which give money for a public purpose instead of buying goods or services, recorded for places in the municipality in a fiscal year. They are money promised, not money spent. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan holds most of the grant dollars that name a municipality, and in some years more than half of the island's grant dollars name no municipality.
economy.fed_grants.es: Subvenciones federales, que dan dinero para un fin público en vez de comprar bienes o servicios, registradas para lugares del municipio en un año fiscal. Son dinero prometido, no gastado. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, San Juan tiene la mayor parte de los dólares de subvenciones que nombran un municipio, y en algunos años más de la mitad de los dólares de subvenciones de la isla no nombran ningún municipio.

economy.fed_direct_payments.en: Money the federal government committed to pay straight to recipients, for example through benefit programs rather than a grant or a loan, recorded for places in the municipality in a fiscal year. It is money promised, not money spent. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is the largest of the five groups in 17 of the 18 years.
economy.fed_direct_payments.es: Dinero que el gobierno federal se comprometió a pagar directamente a quienes lo reciben, por ejemplo mediante programas de beneficios y no mediante una subvención o un préstamo, registrado para lugares del municipio en un año fiscal. Es dinero prometido, no gastado. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 es el mayor de los cinco grupos en 17 de los 18 años.

economy.fed_loans.en: This is what the federal government expects its loans and loan guarantees to cost, for loans recorded in a municipality in one fiscal year (October to September). A loan guarantee is a promise to repay a lender if a borrower does not pay. The value is not the amount lent. It can be negative: in the 2026-10 snapshot the Puerto Rico value is negative in four of the 18 years.
economy.fed_loans.es: Lo que el gobierno federal espera que le cuesten sus préstamos y garantías de préstamo, para los préstamos registrados en un municipio en un año fiscal (de octubre a septiembre). Una garantía de préstamo es la promesa de pagarle a un prestamista si quien tomó el préstamo no paga. El valor no es la cantidad prestada. Puede ser negativo: en el corte de datos de 2026-10, el valor de Puerto Rico es negativo en cuatro de los 18 años.

economy.fed_other.en: Federal insurance and other aid that is not a contract, grant, direct payment or loan, recorded for places in the municipality in a fiscal year. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Adjuntas holds about 90% to 94% of this group's dollars from FY2009 to FY2013, and the data do not say why.
economy.fed_other.es: Seguros federales y otras ayudas que no son contratos, subvenciones, pagos directos ni préstamos, registrados para lugares del municipio en un año fiscal. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Adjuntas tiene entre el 90% y el 94% de los dólares de este grupo en los años fiscales 2009-2013, y los datos no dicen por qué.

economy.fed_place_of_performance.en: USAspending records each award where the awarding agency says the work is done or the benefit goes. Awards for the whole island are often recorded in San Juan, so San Juan's figures can include money meant for other places and other municipalities' figures can be low. The Puerto Rico figure is the territory total, which also counts awards that name no municipality.
economy.fed_place_of_performance.es: USAspending registra cada adjudicación donde la agencia que la otorga dice que se hace el trabajo o llega el beneficio. Las adjudicaciones para toda la isla a menudo se registran en San Juan, así que las cifras de San Juan pueden incluir dinero destinado a otros lugares y las de otros municipios pueden quedar bajas. La cifra de Puerto Rico es el total del territorio, que también cuenta las adjudicaciones que no nombran un municipio.

economy.fema_pa_obligated.en: After a disaster, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) approves money to clear debris and repair public buildings, roads and utilities. This is the federal share of that money, by municipality and by the year the disaster was declared. It is money approved. It does not show damage, need, finished repairs or spending. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 11% to 88% of each year's money is recorded as statewide. No municipality is named for that money.
economy.fema_pa_obligated.es: Después de un desastre, FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) aprueba dinero para remover escombros y reparar edificios públicos, carreteras y servicios públicos. Esta es la parte federal de ese dinero, por municipio y por el año en que se declaró el desastre. Es dinero aprobado. No muestra daños, necesidad, reparaciones terminadas ni gastos. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, entre el 11% y el 88% del dinero de cada año está registrado como estatal. Ese dinero no tiene un municipio asignado.

economy.fema_pa_statewide_share.en: Out of every 100 dollars of Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance federal share for a year's disasters, how many are recorded as statewide and so cannot be placed in a municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot it ranges from 11.0% to 88.3%, and is 80.9% for 2017.
economy.fema_pa_statewide_share.es: De cada 100 dólares de la parte federal de la Asistencia Pública de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) para los desastres de un año, cuántos están registrados como estatales y por eso no se pueden ubicar en un municipio. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 va de 11.0% a 88.3%, y es 80.9% para 2017.

housing.fema_ia_households.en: The number of households FEMA (the Federal Emergency Management Agency) approved for help after disasters declared in a given year, by municipality. It counts approvals, not damage. It does not show how many homes were hurt or how much help people needed.
housing.fema_ia_households.es: El número de hogares que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) aprobó para recibir ayuda después de los desastres declarados en un año dado, por municipio. Cuenta aprobaciones, no daños. No muestra cuántas viviendas sufrieron daños ni cuánta ayuda necesitaba la gente.

housing.fema_ia_amount.en: The dollars the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) approved for households after disasters declared in a given year, by municipality. It shows aid approved, not damage and not necessarily money paid out.
housing.fema_ia_amount.es: Los dólares que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) aprobó para hogares después de los desastres declarados en un año dado, por municipio. Muestra la ayuda aprobada, no los daños, y no necesariamente el dinero pagado.

Whole Community Resilience Planning (WCRP)

The program description is Foundation for Puerto Rico's. The communities are the 79 points of the observatory's WCRP layer (FPR program list, 2026-10-06); each point is approximate, because the plans map their area only in a PDF.

The Risk and Vulnerability Indicators (RVI) rank Puerto Rico's barrios in six areas (economy, education, environment, health, housing and infrastructure) and overall. Each rank is a fifth of the barrios: 1 is the fifth that is least vulnerable on the inputs used, 5 the fifth that is most. Choose an area and a version; click a barrio for its ranks in both versions and the inputs behind them.
WCRP communities
Overall. The six area percentiles are added with equal weights and the sum is ranked again.
Ranks. The index is cut in fifths: 1 (0 to 0.20, low), 2 (medium-low), 3 (medium), 4 (medium-high), 5 (above 0.80, high). Barrios with no residents have no value (14 in the original).
A rank compares barrios with each other on the inputs used. It is not a measure of need, risk of harm or eligibility for any program.

Survey estimates for barrios are rough. Many barrios have few households in the sample, so a barrio near the edge of a fifth can move a rank from one survey period to the next. Read ranks for groups of barrios, not for one barrio alone.

Out of {n} barrios ranked in both versions, {changed}% have a different overall rank in the rebuild and {moved}% move two ranks or more. The table gives each area.

Applied to the original's own published inputs, the method as written here should give back the original's published index. It does for overall, education, health, housing and infrastructure: the order of the barrios is the same (rank correlation 1.00) and almost every barrio keeps its rank. It does not for economy and environment, whose published inputs do not give back their published index; the white paper does not explain the difference. Housing matches when its three inputs are added together, not as the two sub-indicators the white paper describes.

Mislabeled comparison columns. The dashboard compares each barrio with its municipio and with Puerto Rico. In the economy panel the municipio column shows unemployment under the label "public assistance", public assistance under "poverty" and poverty under "unemployed", and the Puerto Rico column shows {pa}% (public assistance) as poverty, which is {pov}%. The housing panel's municipio column is shifted too. The barrio values are labeled correctly. This page shows only barrio values.

Lead-paint shares above 100%. The municipio values of the lead-paint indicator (homes built before 1960) run from {lo}% to {hi}%; {n} municipio values are above 100%, which is impossible for a share. The barrio values used in the index are all at or below 100%.
Homes built before 1990. The share reaches {max}% in {n} barrios of the original.

No license. The ArcGIS services that publish the original state no license or access terms (their license and access fields are empty). Community assets of the Comunidades Especiales, by municipio

The WCRP Social Capital Mapping list records, for each Comunidad Especial, whether it has a community center, a library, an electronic library, a passive park, a sports court, a residents' association, a recreation association, a crime-prevention association and a PDI. The list does not state its date; it was compiled for the program about 2019–2021 from the Junta de Planificación inventory, and no newer source exists. "PDI" is the list's own column name and is not defined there. Click a Comunidad Especial on the map for its own flags.
No road leads from this barrio to a general hospital: its health rank uses the other two inputs.

Four things move the ranks. First, the method does not give back the original's economy and environment indices from their own inputs, and the rebuild leaves out one input (next section): ranking the original's own 2015–2019 values with the rebuild's inputs changes {fewer}% of overall ranks, almost all through economy and environment. Second, several inputs now come from newer sources that define them differently. Third, five years passed. Fourth, survey estimates for barrios are rough: the rebuild run on two survey periods that share two years ({older} and {w}), with the same values for the inputs that are not from the survey, gives a different overall rank to {older_pct}% of barrios. Hunter College built the RVI for Foundation for Puerto Rico's WCRP program and described it in a white paper (December 2021); the dashboard data were published in March 2022. The observatory rebuilds it with the same method on the latest five-year Census survey and on current EPA, housing, street and hospital data.

Percentiles. Each input becomes a percentile among the barrios that have a value: the share of those barrios with a lower value, from 0 to 1. A higher percentile always means more vulnerable (for example, more poverty or fewer homes with internet; for street intersections, fewer intersections).

Areas. Within an area, the percentiles of its inputs are added and the sum is ranked again among the barrios. Infrastructure first groups its inputs in two parts (telecommunications and transportation), each ranked, then adds the two. The white paper describes housing in two parts too, but the published housing index is the plain sum of its three inputs (see the check below), so the rebuild adds them. A barrio that lacks one input gets the sum of the inputs it has, scaled up to the full number: the white paper's rule for education, where 21 barrios with nobody aged 3 to 24 have their no-diploma percentile doubled.

The rebuild leaves out one input that has no current source (solid waste facilities other than landfills), and several inputs come from newer sources that define them differently. The table above says which.

Puerto Rico maps the assessment units of its rivers as the land that drains to each assessed reach, so a listed unit covers a watershed and far more barrios touch one than in the original, which does not say how it drew the waters. The input separates barrios less than the original's.
EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program lists municipal solid waste landfills only (open or closed), not open dumps; the original's landfill or open dump layer was supplied by FPR.
Only the facilities the Facility Registry Service marks active are counted, far fewer than the original counted; it does not say which it took.
Areas still in non-attainment in the EPA Green Book: San Juan and Guayama-Salinas for sulfur dioxide, Arecibo for lead.
CHAS is published for census tracts, not barrios: the barrio value is an estimate, the tract counts spread by 2020 housing units. 2016–2020 is the newest window a script may read.

Intersections where three or more street edges meet (TIGER/Line 2026; no highways, ramps or paths) over land area. The original counted TIGER 2020 roads in a way it does not describe, so only the order of the barrios compares, not the values.

WCRP helps communities in Puerto Rico design their own resilience plans: they set their vision, needs and goals, and plan, run and follow up the work to reach them. Foundation for Puerto Rico runs the program in collaboration with the Puerto Rico Department of Housing (PRDOH), with Community Development Block Grant – Disaster Recovery (CDBG-DR) funds from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), as part of the Action Plan that HUD approved.
